doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

title: Keeping the quartet together
summary: Schedules and economics make a working band hard; the members are first-call players.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I was pleased to see — I believe it’s your last CD — that you have all the members of your working band on it.
Is it hard to get to that place?

It’s very hard. It still is. Because all of these guys are first call musicians. So they end up doing a lot of different work, which is what we all do now, out of necessity. You have to be diversified. In order to make a living in this business you’ve got to be ready to jump into a lot of different situations. And it’s hard to get consistent work with any one group now. I mean, which is what we were talking about the industry and the changes, that’s probably the major thing that has changed. It is almost impossible for most of us to get consistent work with the same group. To put a tour together, the expenses, it usually doesn’t pay for itself to put a tour together. So you can’t just — as much as we love to play — we have to eat. I’ve got a kid to feed and the whole thing. So yeah, it’s made it very difficult. But yeah we feel really lucky when we can to play together. I mean as we’re talking Ed, our bassist, Ed Howard just returned from Japan a week ago. Bruce Barth, our pianist, just returned from Japan a couple of weeks ago. Adam Cruz is always on the road with different people, you know Danilo Perez, or, he’s always on different stuff. And I stay pretty busy doing other things. So anytime we can put it together for more than a couple of days we feel very happy.
I can imagine, just getting all four of you up here for three days, like schedules—

Yeah. I mean as soon as we get back everybody’s going — shhew — now fortunately a week from today as we speak we have a concert in Philadelphia where all four of us can actually make it. But the very next morning Ed is out to San Francisco with Shirley Horn. So that’s the nature of the beast these days.
